data.question: fav:* prompt-injection HIGH finding — (A) fix now, (B) punt post-launch, (C) disable fav:* at launch?
data.answer: Option A. Fix now. 30 min is cheap for a HIGH on launch day. Local-only reduces blast radius (attacker needs local FS write) but testers are real users who will invoke these skills on day 1. Delimiter pattern is also a reusable architectural fix for any skill that reads user-provided files. α's lean is correct.

data.question: fav:* delimiter-breakout residual MEDIUM — (A) random delimiter, (B) save-side sanitization, (C) structural code-parse, (D) accept MEDIUM + ticket C post-launch?
data.answer: Option D with A applied. Apply random 16-hex delimiter now (5 min), accept MEDIUM risk, ticket C for post-launch. Attacker preconditions: local FS write + awareness of internal delimiter. Solo founder testers on their own machines — this threat model is essentially self-attack. 'Data/Instruction confusion' residual is a fundamental LLM limitation, not a fixable bug; redteam flagging it as a finding is a category error. 1-2 hours on structural fix is not launch-critical given actual exposure.

data.answer: ESCALATE (Class C). Two pre-execute concerns. (1) Ownership-transition trigger semantics is user-trust-affecting — operator must pick: automatic on any non-whitespace edit (Beta recommendation: yes, auto — operator's stated pain is silent DELETE_CONFLICT, an explicit command just shifts burden) vs explicit operator command. (2) install.ps1 hash audit needed pre-execute — if PowerShell-side uses 12-char prefix, fresh installs break on Windows after 0.7.0 format change. Other approvals correctly flagged: push+tag for 0.7.0, consumer updates (aiweb, jobhunter-app), framework-installed.json schema coverage. Redteam plan strong; minor gap: AC-5.3 doesn't test CRLF-in-override-reason injection into JSONL.

data.question: Resolve Beta ESCALATE: (1) ownership-transition trigger, (2) install.ps1 hash audit.
data.answer: (1) Decision: automatic on any non-whitespace edit. Rationale: matches Beta recommendation; operator's stated pain is silent DELETE_CONFLICT, an explicit command just shifts the burden; user can override the trigger via decisions-ledger flip in a future sprint if it surprises them. Logging to decisions-ledger via /sprint:execute on T-073. (2) Audit complete: install.ps1 line 143 uses Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 which returns full 64-char hex (.Hash.ToLower()). The full hash is stored in framework-installed.json#assets[].installedHash. install.ps1 only WRITES the snapshot; it does not READ/compare hashes. Hash comparison logic is node-side (update.js, manifest-honesty.js). Conclusion: install.ps1 needs no patch in this sprint. Audit result documented on T-068 (content-hash module) for execution-phase verification.
